root_cause.text: In the RCU read-unlock path, commit 5f5fa7ea89dc removed __rcu_read_unlock() recursion protection, allowing rcu_read_unlock_special() to re-enter via trace-triggered softirq raising because raise_softirq_irqoff(RCU_SOFTIRQ) was called without first marking deferred QS work as already pending in rcu_data.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says the deadloop started after “remov[ing] the recursion-protection code from __rcu_read_unlock()”, and the fix adds a guard in rcu_read_unlock_special() to set `rdp->defer_qs_pending = DEFER_QS_PENDING` before `raise_softirq_irqoff(RCU_SOFTIRQ)` (mirroring the earlier IRQ-work fix) so repeated re-entry cannot loop.

intent_record.intent_summary: Rename the deferred quiescent-state pending flag and update its comment to reflect that it covers both irq_work and softirq pending work.
intent_record.what: The field name in struct rcu_data was changed from defer_qs_iw_pending to defer_qs_pending, and its comment was updated from indicating only pending scheduler attention to indicating either irq_work or softirq is pending.
intent_record.how: This broadens the documented meaning of the flag from tracking only irq_work-based deferred quiescent-state handling to tracking pending deferred quiescent-state work from either irq_work or softirq paths, clarifying and likely aligning the variable with its actual runtime use.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix rcu_preempt_deferred_qs_irqrestore() to clear the correct deferred quiescent-state pending flag.
intent_record.what: The code in rcu_preempt_deferred_qs_irqrestore() was changed to read and write the rcu_data field defer_qs_pending instead of defer_qs_iw_pending when checking for DEFER_QS_PENDING and resetting the state to DEFER_QS_IDLE.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes the function clear the regular deferred quiescent-state pending flag rather than a different iw-specific flag, so the correct pending state is reset when this path runs and deferred quiescent-state handling can proceed consistently.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix deferred QS state handling by clearing the correct pending flag when preemption depth prevents reporting.
intent_record.what: The code changes the WRITE_ONCE() target in rcu_preempt_deferred_qs_handler() from rdp->defer_qs_iw_pending to rdp->defer_qs_pending when rcu_preempt_depth() > 0, leaving the assigned value DEFER_QS_IDLE unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the handler now resets the deferred quiescent-state pending flag field instead of a different similarly named field, ensuring the correct state variable is updated when deferred QS reporting cannot proceed due to preempt depth being greater than zero.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid redundant RCU softirq raises by marking deferred quiescent-state work as pending before scheduling it.
intent_record.what: The unconditional call to raise_softirq_irqoff(RCU_SOFTIRQ) inside rcu_read_unlock_special() was replaced with a conditional block that first checks whether rdp->defer_qs_pending is not equal to DEFER_QS_PENDING, then sets rdp->defer_qs_pending to DEFER_QS_PENDING and raises RCU_SOFTIRQ only in that case.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents repeatedly raising the RCU softirq when a deferred quiescent-state request is already pending, ensuring the pending state is recorded once before scheduling the softirq and avoiding redundant softirq wakeups for the same deferred work.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the correct deferred quiescent-state pending flag when queueing RCU IRQ work in `rcu_read_unlock_special()`.
intent_record.what: The code replaces accesses to the per-CPU RCU field `rdp->defer_qs_iw_pending` with `rdp->defer_qs_pending` in both the conditional check and the assignment before calling `irq_work_queue_on()` inside `rcu_read_unlock_special()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the deferred quiescent-state pending flag is now checked and set using `defer_qs_pending` instead of `defer_qs_iw_pending`, ensuring this path uses the intended state variable to avoid duplicate or missed deferred QS scheduling when queueing IRQ work.

Use the correct deferred quiescent-state pending flag when queueing RCU IRQ work in `rcu_read_unlock_special()`.

consistency_review.core_intent: Correct deferred RCU quiescent-state pending flag handling and scheduling in the preemptible RCU unlock/deferred-QS path.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is specifically about deferred QS work not being marked pending before raising RCU softirq, enabling re-entry. Renaming the pending flag and clarifying that it covers both irq_work and softirq pending work directly relates to that root cause and the affected state tracking.

The changes directly address the deferred quiescent-state pending flag logic in the RCU read-unlock/deferred-QS path, including marking work as pending before raising/scheduling RCU softirq/IRQ work. That matches the root cause: missing pending-state protection allowed re-entry of rcu_read_unlock_special() after recursion protection was removed.

candidates.rationale: This directly embodies the root cause: the RCU softirq is raised from the read-unlock path without first marking deferred QS work as pending, allowing trace-triggered re-entry into rcu_read_unlock_special() after recursion protection was removed.

This flag is the state that should have been set before raising the softirq. Its existence and intended role are central to the bug, because failure to mark it pending permitted duplicate/re-entrant deferred-QS scheduling.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement raises the RCU softirq from the RCU read-unlock path without first marking deferred quiescent-state work as already pending in rcu_data. After recursion protection in __rcu_read_unlock() was removed, that allowed trace-induced softirq activity to re-enter rcu_read_unlock_special(), which is the root cause described.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact control flow around the vulnerable operation in the RCU read-unlock special handling path. The root cause says the bug occurs when `raise_softirq_irqoff(RCU_SOFTIRQ)` is invoked without first marking deferred QS work as already pending in `rcu_data`, which can allow re-entry into `rcu_read_unlock_special()`. In this function, when `irqs_were_disabled` is true, the code executes `raise_softirq_irqoff(RCU_SOFTIRQ);` at line 650 after only clearing `t->rcu_read_unlock_special.b.exp_hint` at line 646. There is no visible statement before line 650 that marks deferred quiescent-state work as pending in `rcu_data` (for example via a flag/field update preventing re-entry). Therefore the vulnerable construct is present. Because the required pending-state update is absent, the fix is not yet present.
